learning_outcomes.text: The student possesses the analytical and numerical techniques for simulating acoustics problems.
The student is familiar with and capable of applying the finite difference technique for spatial discretisation of the Laplacian and biharmonic operators in one and two dimensions.
The student is familiar with and capable of applying the finite difference technique for temporal derivative discretisation.
The student is familiar with and capable of applying analytical tools for constructing numerical schemes for simulating wave equations in cables, bars, plates, and membranes.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to finite differences. Construction of finite difference operators via Taylor series. Truncation error and order of accuracy.
Laplacian and biharmonic operators. Definitions, examples of typical acoustic and vibroacoustic problems. Boundary value problems. Eigenvalues and eigenfunctions. Modal representation.

Discretization of the Laplacian and biharmonic operators with various boundary conditions. Examples in one and two dimensions. Cartesian grids, with a brief introduction to polar grids in 2D for circular geometries.
Lagrange interpolation. Use of Cartesian grids for problems with non-rectangular geometry.
Numerical computation of eigenvalues and eigenfunctions of the Laplacian and biharmonic operators for problems with and without analytical solutions.
Wave propagation. One- and two-dimensional models. Equations for strings, rods, membranes, and plates. 2D acoustics, visualization of the acoustic field.
Finite differences in time. Harmonic oscillator. Explicit and implicit schemes. Truncation error and frequency distortion. Exact schemes. Application to wave propagation problems. Stability.
Introduction to nonlinear acoustic problems. Duffing oscillator, nonlinear wave equation.
assessment_rules: The exam is project-based. Each student will work independently and submit a Matlab project, to be discussed with the lecturer during an oral exam. To finalise the assessment, the lecturer may ask further questions during the exam.
